name: Prompt–Intent–Goal Alignment
status: v0 PROTOTYPE — no scoring run exists yet; the behavior matrix and expectation labels are preregistered single-author design choices with zero validity evidence. Not part of the CAIMS composite.
measurement_target: Displayed ambiguity-handling behavior: whether a response to an underspecified prompt engages the plausible intent space, and whether it clarifies, states an assumption, or commits silently — evaluated against the stakes declared for the item
observable: An LLM judge's CLASSIFICATION of the response (intents addressed, one of five behavior classes); the judge produces no scores. The number is a fixed, versioned function of that classification. What is observed is text behavior — not the model's actual representation of user intent
instrument: Judge-as-classifier (prompt fingerprint PIGA_PROMPT_HASH) + deterministic scoring matrix PIGA_BEHAVIOR_MATRIX with declared weights (coverage 0.35 / behavior 0.65), protocol 0.1.0-alpha

coverage.observes: fraction of the item's declared plausible intents the response engaged with, as classified

behavior.observes: clarify-vs-assume decision class, mapped through the preregistered matrix for the item's declared expectation stratum

theory_inspiration: Gricean pragmatics / speech-act ambiguity (inspiration only, not an implementation): no formal pragmatic model is computed
Theory-of-mind evaluation literature (inspiration only, not an implementation): PIGA classifies displayed disambiguation behavior; it does not test or claim mental-state attribution
allowed_claims: Model X's responses were classified as clarifying on N of M high-stakes-ambiguous items under judge configuration Z
PIGA is process-scored: a silently-guessed correct intent scores the same as a silently-guessed wrong one, and the guess outcome is recorded separately, never scored
The scoring layer is deterministic given a classification: identical classifications always yield identical scores
prohibited_claims: The model understood / read / reconstructed the user's intent (PIGA observes response text, not intent representations)
PIGA measures theory of mind, empathy, or any mental capacity
PIGA scores are comparable across protocol versions or across judge configurations without an agreement analysis
The expectation labels (required/acceptable/unnecessary) are ground truth (they are single-author judgments pending human annotation)
known_confounds: Single-turn confound: a subject model may cover all intents instead of asking BECAUSE the protocol is single-turn and no answer to a question would ever arrive; the matrix therefore scores answered_all_intents 70-75, but the ask-vs-branch choice partially reflects the deployment format, not disposition
Judge classification reliability is UNMEASURED (no 2-judge run yet); the deterministic layer removes numeric judge freedom but classification disagreement propagates fully into scores
Expectation labels and intent spaces are authored by one person; a different author would draw different intent spaces, which changes coverage denominators
Subject models whose system prompts or RLHF training push clarification-seeking will score high on 'required' items for reasons unrelated to this prompt's ambiguity (policy, not perception)
The behavior matrix values (100/35/70/45/0 etc.) are design choices; ordinal claims (asked_specific > asked_generic) are defended in the spec, but the cardinal gaps are arbitrary
negative_controls: 'unnecessary' stratum (piga-specified-rename, piga-specified-email): fully specified prompts where asking is over-asking — a blanket 'always clarify' policy scores 20/5 on behavior there
asked_generic class: a contentless 'could you clarify?' is structurally capped (30-35) far below engaged clarification on every stratum
positive_controls: none — no PIGA run exists yet; the first run must publish per-stratum results including failures
statistics: per-item score 0-100 from the deterministic matrix; per-stratum means; no aggregate PIGA index is defined in v0 and no significance claims are possible with 12 items

validity_evidence.content: intent spaces, expectation labels, and rationales authored per item and reviewed adversarially in-repo; single-author, no expert panel and no human annotation yet — a Phase B task
validity_evidence.discriminant: none — no runs yet; planned check: PIGA should NOT correlate strongly with fluency-driven composite scores on the same responses
validity_evidence.reliability: none measured — the deterministic layer guarantees score reproducibility GIVEN a classification, but judge classification agreement (nominal-scale alpha on behavior classes across >=2 judge families) is unmeasured until a 2-judge run exists

validity_domain: English single-turn prompts; v0 items are workplace/software-flavored; nothing is claimed for multi-turn dialogue, other languages, or domains outside the 12 authored items
